newsitem.title: ITALY: Forget Milan -- Versace eyes London's style oasis.
newsitem.headline: Forget Milan -- Versace eyes London's style oasis.

text.p: Italy's Gianni Versace borrowed from Britain for inspiration for his latest Istante womenswear collection on Tuesday, looking to streetwise London to take the cloying element out of faintly frilly designs.

With images of Buckingham Palace guards in high bearskin hats projected on to the walls of his elegant Milan palazzo, Versace launched his second line's 1997 spring/summer ready-to-wear designs to the sounds of British rock group Oasis.

"When Savile Row becomes Savile Rock...London uses its imagination in a new language, more energetic, more modern," Versace said, unveiling high-waisted, A-line skirted mini-sun dresses in demure grey, vivid yellow and hallmark purple.

Hems were scallopped or lightly frilly, while pinafore sundresses had frilled shoulder straps and necklines sometimes in contrasting colours, with the whole look finished off by high-heels and schoolgirl-like dark ankle socks.
But Versace did not desert the curvaceous, using monotone and horizontally striped figure-hugging jersey dresses to enhance the female form.

Daring transparency was also on the agenda. Filmy black evening tops had a camisole underlay for the fainthearted and nothing for the brave, while models wore high-fitting black gym-style knickers beneath gauzy black skirts.
Earlier Miuccia Prada overturned convention when she set transparent chiffon over linen and silk underskirts, giving the appearance of clothing worn inside out.
"The underskirt becomes a skirt and vice versa, the jacket becomes a shirt, the under can be over," Prada said.

Cream underskirts were overlaid with gauzy blues, blood or wine reds and moss greens and set off either by platform wedge black patent-leather sandals or light-hued, high-heeled shoes decorated with a darker vine motif and clasped at the ankle.
Lengths varied, with straight underskirts long or mini and overlaid with longer sheathes of chiffon, while hemlines on some poplin skirts dropped lower behind and fanned into a tail.
Blouses were either entirely transparent or backed by camisole tops with "the demure and the immodest alternating... The lingerie is an integrating part of the transparent".
Short nightdress-style frocks scooped out at the neckline and trimmed with a small frill were on offer with the top layer in one shade of red and the underlay in another.

For evening there were rich embroideries, demure dark vines and willow-leaf patterns set on light backgrounds and full-length mandarin-collared tunics slit up both sides to reveal shimmering light golden underskirts.
Design house Byblos provided a bright and bubbly contrast with a collection of fluorescent lime greens, fuchsia and orange in slip dresses, tailored jackets and close-fitting minis.

Models wore black off-the-shoulder minis and long sheathes trimmed at low necklines with black feathers, filmy apricot or coral slips with lacy, scallopped hems and red tights as well as outfits with a hotter toned orange, green and red flower print.
The shows continue on Wednesday with design duo Dolce & Gabbana and stylist Krizia and fashion house Gucci and designer Gianfranco Ferre on Thursday and Friday.
Versace presents his main collection on Saturday and Giorgio Armani closes the shows with his top line Giorgio Armani label on Sunday.
